newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges minimal regulation of Internet.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges minimal regulation of Internet.

text.p: Hailing the potential of the Internet as an engine for economic growth, U.S. President Bill Clinton on Tuesday unveiled a comprehensive policy to promote commerce in cyberspace that unfetters the private sector.

At a White House ceremony at which the new policy was announced, Vice President Al Gore said that if the government were to heavily regulate "something that has spawned changes so quickly and so often, we risk suffocating the very essence of the Internet."

Clinton said the high-speed computer network, which links individuals, businesses, schools, libraries, governments and other institutions throughout the world, can be an engine for U.S. exports and job growth in the 21st century.
"We hope to harness its full potential for increasing productivity and growing the economy, bringing prosperity to the American people and individuals worldwide," he said.
Like much of his second-term agenda, Clinton's Internet policy contemplates only modest government involvement.

Commerce over the Internet, which includes sales of everything from books and compact disks to fine wine and cheese, is projected to grow from less than $1 billion last year to perhaps $5 billion to $10 billion by the year 2000.
